pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
QUEST FOR THE ROUND TUIT

A Realm of Procrastia Adventure

In the Kingdom of Procrastia, everything gets done. Eventually. The castle in Laterburg has been waiting forty years for its roof. The bridge at Eventually Falls was started in the reign of King Dillydally VI. The Royal Library's overdue notices are themselves overdue.

What keeps the realm turning at all is the Royal Round Tuit: an old oak disc ringed in brass, kept on the Tuit Table in the Garden Court. Whenever a King of Procrastia gets a round tuit, he gets around to it. That's the law.

Then Lord Deadline, who hates a thing put off more than anything in the world, stole the Round Tuit, broke it in three and hid the pieces: one under the Snooze Barrows, one in the Soggy Vaults, one in the Putoff Mines. Without it, nobody in Procrastia gets around to anything. Least of all stopping him.

Nobody, that is, except Pip, the stable hand of Nowish, who does things the very day he's asked. His grandmother is very proud. And a little worried.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TUIT and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized sound effects; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

Pick Play from the menu. Leave the menu alone and the game plays itself for a while: a good way to see how fighting works. Read Storyline tells the tale so far; Read Instructions is a short version of this manual.

Your satchel

There's nothing on the screen but Procrastia. Press F2 to open your satchel: it shows your gold, your hit points, your lives and what you carry. Save your game with F5 and load it with F6. Procrastia is bigger than it looks.

Hit points and lives

You start with 100 hit points, three lives and a single tonic. Foes bite; tonics, hearts, inn beds and the occasional pot put you right. Lose all your hit points and you start the place you're in over (with your gold and everything you've found still yours); lose all your lives and Lord Deadline wins. For now.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

↑ ↓ ← →
or W A S D		Walk. Walk into people to talk to them, into counters to buy, into gates to open them.
SpaceSwing your sword the way you last walked. To face a boss (you can't walk into one), tap the arrow toward it, then swing. Once you own a steel sword, Space swings steel.
ZToot the Kazoo of Haste (once Doc Leo has taught you): a note flies straight ahead and beats nearly anything.
TDrink a tonic: 40 hit points.
EnterPick up what you're standing on. Hardly anything in Procrastia can be picked up. Hardly.
F1Help
F2Your satchel: gold, hit points, lives, what you carry
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load
EscQuit to the menu

Driving THE CHEZ

On the Dawdle Flats the arrows drive (briskly) and Space squeezes the horn: its ah-OOO-gah flies ahead like a kazoo note and clears crabs off the causeway. Your hit points are the carriage's charge. Charging posts top it up.

pages.head: Townsfolk and Shops
pages.html:
Townsfolk and Shops

To talk to someone, walk into them. They'll have their say and you'll be standing just where you were. Talk to everyone: Procrastians know a great deal and get around to telling you most of it.

Shopping

Market stalls sell from their counters. Walk into a counter once to pay, and again to take what you bought. If you can't afford it, the counter won't budge.

Shops only keep a few of anything in stock. Leave town and come back; they'll have restocked. Eventually.

pages.head: The Kingdom
pages.html:
The Kingdom of Procrastia

Two lands across the Dawdle Flats, forty leagues of tidal mud nobody has ever finished walking.

Dallydale (the west)

  • Nowish: Pip's village. Population: some.
  • Laterburg: the capital. The Garden Court (roof pending), the market, the Procrastinating Pony, the Royal Library, the royal kennel.
  • Someday Harbor: on the west coast. The lighthouse, the long pier, the fishing pier, and Professor Fiddlesticks' garage.
  • The Whistling Woods, east of the River Dither, and Lake Later.

Far Putoff (the east)

  • Eventually Falls: a river town under a waterfall. Hattie's General Store, Doc Leo's tent, Foreman Duff.
  • Mount Putoff and its mines.
  • The Gloomwood, and in it Deadline Keep, where every clock has stopped at a minute to midnight.

pages.head: Old Procrastian
pages.html:
Old Procrastian

The old Procrastians carved their advice into floors, doors and anything else that would hold still, in runes nobody has read for four hundred years. Nobody got around to it.

The Royal Code Wheel reads them. Every carving begins with its key, set in brass: a letter, then a rune. Turn the small disc until the key's rune sits against the key's letter on the big disc. Now each rune of the carving sits against the letter it stands for. A blank stone is a gap between words.

Step on a carving's brass key to kneel and read it close up. Then take your time: the runes aren't going anywhere. They never have.

The miners' marks

The miners of Mount Putoff used the wheel's three windows. Set a key and the windows show three marks, 1, 2 and 3 from left to right. Miners hung their doors with marks, too. They meant to tell you why.

pages.head: Foes
pages.html:
Foes

Foes come at you when you're near. A bite hurts you, but it hurts them too. Two blows finish most of them; they leave a gem behind (5 gold, or a ruby worth 20). Some things in Procrastia leave hearts.

FoeWhereNotes
ProcrastislimeEverywhereWill attack you later. Later is usually now.
Snooze BatThe hills, the Barrows, the MinesQuick. One blow.
Barrow GhostThe Snooze BarrowsDrifts through rock. Wait for it to come out.
Tide CrabThe Vaults, the FlatsSideways, always. On the Flats some patrol the causeway, back and forth on a beat.
Bog EelThe Vaults' poolsLeaps from pool to pool.
Rust GolemThe Putoff MinesThree blows.
Gloom Goblin, Clockwork TickDeadline Keep (goblins also on the road south of Eventually Falls)The Keep's staff. Underpaid. On time.

Bosses

Each piece of the Tuit is guarded by someone two blocks tall who would rather be asleep: Sir Snoozalot, the Barrow King; the Kraken of Kinda-Later; Tick-Tock the Unpunctual; and Lord Deadline himself. Your wooden sword won't scratch the last three: buy steel. Bosses sit in the way. Swing until they aren't.

Lord Deadline

His clockwork armor is only the first half of the fight. Break it and Lord Deadline steps out on foot, sword up. He backs off a few paces, then charges straight at you, twice, before he backs away to think about it. Every moment he touches you costs hit points. Face the way he's coming and swing as he arrives, then step aside. Six good blows and he's done. The foes grow fiercer the deeper you go, so rest at an inn before the Keep.

pages.head: Hints
pages.html:
Hints from the Royal Library

  • Gates open for the right thing in your satchel: the Royal Writ (the Barrows), the foghorn (the fog bank on Someday Harbor's long pier), a lamp (the Mines), something with lightning in it (THE CHEZ's garage) and all three pieces (the Keep). Walk into them.
  • The King hands out writs to anyone who asks. Have two.
  • The Tuit Table in the Garden Court lights a pedestal for each piece you carry. A good way to check.
  • On the Dawdle Flats, the two low bridges flood with the tide. The tide pole beside each one counts it down: the water climbs the marks, the flag goes red, then the bridge is under. Wait for it to go out.
  • The rivers can't be swum. Look for bridges.
  • Shops restock whenever you come back to town.
  • Save before every boss.
  • Doc Leo's kazoo note beats nearly anything, but each toot costs a reed.
  • Runes in the floor? Step on the brass key in front of them to read them close up, and set the Royal Code Wheel by it.
  • Waterfalls are mostly water.

Stuck? The Royal Hint Book answers everything, under a sheet of red film. Free with registration.

pages.head: Credits
pages.html:
Credits

Design, pixels, maps, music, sound and words: Claude, at Sandbox Software. Every block, monster, song and scene is a real Game-Maker 3.0 file, built in code.

The shores, rivers and roads of Procrastia are autotiles: each block is chosen by which of its four corners lie in water, road, wood or rock, and each was painted in full color with antialiased edges, foam, wet sand and shadows, then dithered into the scene's 256-color palette.

Starring

  • Doc Leo, hobo clown, PhD (Comedic Science), as himself
  • Sir Reginald Cluckington III, a rubber chicken
  • Teddy, a corgi who knows his left from his right
  • Gwinn
  • THE CHEZ, a 1976½ CitiCar (charge port: rear passenger side)

For Lewis "Lewie" Moten III, who always gets around to it.

Made with GAME-MAKER by Recreational Software Designs.

news.head: Sandbox Software Gets Around to an RPG
news.html: Fans have asked for a role-playing game since our first disk. We said we'd get around to it. Quest for the Round Tuit is that. Four towns, four dungeons, two dozen people to talk to, and coastlines that curve - in Game-Maker, which nobody told us couldn't be done until we'd done it.

news.head: A horseless carriage in Procrastia
news.html: Every kingdom needs a way to get around. Procrastia's is THE CHEZ, a horseless carriage from the far-off future of 1976 and a half, waiting in Professor Fiddlesticks' garage for something with lightning in it. Charge it and drive forty leagues of tidal mud across the Dawdle Flats; its ah-OOO-gah horn clears the crabs off the causeway. Its charge port is on the rear passenger side, as always.

news.head: Since last issue: The box art made the printer
news.html: Depth Perception's box art went to the printer on time, and you've been pulling focus ever since. The trick most of you learned the hard way: a soft, see-through block isn't there right now. The trick most of you learned on the BBS: not every mirror in the Hall of Mirrors is a wall. And yes, registered players, the cardboard glasses are in your box. No, you won't need them.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Royal hounds
news.html: Teddy and Gwinn have royal jobs this time: they're the King's two runaway hounds, and Kennelmaster Bess would like them home. Doc Leo plays himself, as usual, and his rubber chicken finally has a name of its own. Office news: Gwinn sat on command this month. Once. Nobody had a camera, but three of us saw it.

news.head: In the workshop: Where's Gwinn?
news.html: The morning after the Big Show, Gwinn's bed is empty. That's how our next game begins: Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure. Teddy has a new trick, and for the first time in a Sandbox game you'll play as somebody else, too. Somebody big, brown and still learning to sit.

news.head: Letters: "Why ray tracing?"
news.html:
"My dad says ray tracing is for serious computers. Why is it in a game?" - A reader, by modem

The Scoop replies: Because a chrome sphere on a checkerboard is the most beautiful thing a computer can draw. Tell your dad the office 486 agrees, eventually.

items.title: A Royal Decree
items.letterhead: BY ORDER OF HIS MAJESTY KING DILLYDALLY IX
items.to: To whomever gets around to reading this
items.body:
Be it known that the Royal Round Tuit has been stolen by one LORD DEADLINE, who was not invited.

Any subject who returns the three pieces of the Round Tuit to the Tuit Table shall receive Our gratitude, a feast, and a Royal Writ (they are free; have several).

We shall see to the matter personally as soon as We get a round tuit. Which is, you will appreciate, the difficulty.

items.title: The Royal Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Compiled by Ms. Pagely of the Royal Library, who would like her books back. Lay the red film over an answer to read it.

hints.q: Where do I go first?
hints.a: North up the road from Nowish to Laterburg. Walk into the King on his throne at the top of the Garden Court: he gives you the Royal Writ.

hints.q: How do I talk to people?
hints.a: Walk into them.

hints.q: How do I buy things?
hints.a: Walk into the counter once to pay and again to take it. No money, no sale.

hints.q: I'm out of gold.
hints.a: Foes drop gems: 5 gold each, 20 for a ruby. The dungeons have chests. The kennel and the library pay rewards.

hints.q: The door in the Snooze Barrows won't open.
hints.a: It's sealed in the King's name. Get the Royal Writ from King Dillydally first, then walk into the door.

hints.q: How do I reach the Soggy Vaults?
hints.a: Walk out along Someday Harbor's long pier to the fog bank. It only clears for the Harbor Master's foghorn, which is lying in the west room of the Snooze Barrows.

hints.q: My sword bounces off the Kraken.
hints.a: From the Vaults on, bosses are too tough for wood. Buy the steel sword from Brokk in Laterburg's market for 80 gold.

hints.q: How do I get across to Far Putoff?
hints.a: In THE CHEZ. The second piece of the Tuit is full of lightning: carry it to Professor Fiddlesticks' garage in Someday Harbor and walk into the garage door.

hints.q: The bridge on the Flats is under water!
hints.a: It's the tide. Wait a few seconds and it drains again. The striped tide pole beside the bridge tells you when: once its flag goes red, the water is on its way.

hints.q: The Putoff Mines' door won't let me in.
hints.a: It wants a lamp: 40 gold at Hattie's stall in Eventually Falls.

hints.q: Lord Deadline jumped out of his armor!
hints.a: That's his second act. He backs off, then charges straight at you. Face him and swing as he comes, then step aside. Six blows; he leaves a heart.

hints.q: Where is Deadline Keep's door?
hints.a: On the south side of the Keep. The road from Eventually Falls goes round the east side of the Gloomwood to it.

hints.q: The Keep's sockets won't open.
hints.a: Each one wants its piece of the Tuit. If one stays shut, you're missing that piece: the Tuit Table in the Garden Court lights a pedestal for each piece you carry.

hints.q: How do I use the Code Wheel?
hints.a: Every carving starts with a brass letter and a brass rune. Turn the small disc until that rune sits against that letter. Then read each rune of the carving off the big disc.

hints.q: What do the runes in the Snooze Barrows say?
hints.a: Set rune Yawn against P: FOGHORN WEST. The foghorn is in the west room.

hints.q: Which door in the Putoff Mines?
hints.a: The miners' plate says M and rune Putter. Set them, and the windows show bell, lamp, gem: the third door from the west.

hints.q: What do the runes in Deadline Keep say?
hints.a: Set rune Snooze against D: SWING AS HE COMES. It's about Lord Deadline on foot.

hints.q: I picked a cupboard.
hints.a: No harm done: you come out in the passage south of the stopes. Walk back up and try the door the wheel shows you.

hints.q: Where are the royal hounds?
hints.a: Teddy is in a clearing in the Whistling Woods: take the trail east off the north road. Gwinn is digging on the beach south of Someday Harbor. Walk into each, then walk into the kennel gate in the Garden Court.

hints.q: Where is the Tome of Tomorrow?
hints.a: In the Putoff Mines' old workings, west of the great gallery. Take it to the rope at the Royal Library's door.

hints.q: Where is Sir Reginald Cluckington III?
hints.a: In a glade in the Gloomwood, east of the road to Deadline Keep. Walk into him, then into the flap of Doc Leo's tent in Eventually Falls.

hints.q: What does the kazoo do?
hints.a: Press Z. A note flies straight ahead and beats nearly anything, bosses included. Lyra sells reeds in Someday Harbor: ten notes for ten gold.

hints.q: The hermit's garden? What hermit?
hints.a: Eventually Falls has a waterfall at the top of town. Its left side is only spray: walk straight up through it.

hints.q: The nest is empty.
hints.a: Watch it. Every twenty seconds or so something turns up in it for a moment. Stand on the nest and press ENTER while it's there.

hints.q: Just draw me a map.
hints.a: Up the main street to the foot of the falls, through the left edge of the falling water, and into the garden. The nest is right of the hermit; the stone beside it opens for whoever carries the egg.

items.title: The Royal Code Wheel
items.note: Turns Old Procrastian runes into plain letters
items.heading: The Royal Code Wheel of Procrastia · Old Procrastian into plain letters
howto: Every carving in Procrastia begins with its key, set in brass: a letter, then a rune.
Turn the small disc until the key's rune sits against the key's letter on the big disc.
Now read the carving: each rune sits against the letter it stands for. A blank stone is a gap between words.
The three windows show the miners' marks for that key. Marks on a door read left to right: window 1, then 2, then 3.

puzzles.ask: The Snooze Barrows: what do the runes in the floor by the way in say?
puzzles.answer: FOGHORN WEST. The Harbor Master's foghorn lies in the barrow's west room. Take it before you go.

puzzles.ask: The Putoff Mines: which of the four doors in the bulkhead is the true one?
puzzles.answer: The windows show bell, lamp, gem: the third door from the west. The other three are cupboards.

puzzles.ask: Deadline Keep: what do the runes in the Hall of Sockets say?
puzzles.answer: SWING AS HE COMES. When Lord Deadline charges at you on foot, face him and swing as he arrives.
